clue.text: It's the boatman's turn, bottoms up !

definitions.text: It's the boatman's turn, bottoms up !

parts.words: It's the boatman's turn, bottoms up
parts.note: a boat that capsizes so its bottom points skywards is said to make this kind of turn, named after a sea creature

explanation.surface: Someone tells a rower it is their go, with a jolly toast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottoms up' looks like a drinking toast, but it describes a boat's hull rising as it capsizes: the boat is said to 'turn turtle'.
explanation.definitionFit: To capsize is idiomatically to turn turtle, the hull rolling upward like an upturned shell.

clue.text: The edict is Russia's, but sounds like ours

indicators.note: sounds like says the clue word is to be said and heard as another

parts.note: to a British paper, ours means the UK's

explanation.surface: Noting that a Russian decree sounds as if it belongs to us.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the edict is Russia's: a ukase was a tsar's decree. Said out loud, it is 'UK's', and for a British paper 'ours' is the UK's.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree issued by a Russian tsar or government is an official edict.

clue.text: Perhaps a general revision of two acts in one

indicators.note: a revision changes a text around, so these letters are put in a new order
two asks for the act word to appear twice

parts.note: each of the acts is one act
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A general is said to rework a two-act play into a single act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' gives ACT twice; with IN and I, 'revision of' rearranges ACTACTINI.
explanation.definitionFit: A general plans the moves of a battle, the work of a skilled strategist; 'perhaps' marks him as one example.

clue.text: the fair, - -the loveable " (Tennyson)

parts.note: the blanks are the name Tennyson repeats in his Idylls of the King, the lily maid of Astolat

explanation.surface: A fill-in-the-blank quotation from Tennyson's Idylls of the King.
explanation.walkthrough: The line reads 'Elaine the fair, Elaine the loveable, Elaine the lily maid of Astolat' from Tennyson's 'Lancelot and Elaine'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Astolat maiden who loved Lancelot is named in that Tennyson line.

clue.text: Devices for securing lodgings?

parts.note: read as 'lodgings' (slang pad) plus 'devices for securing' (locks), or as lockable fastenings for doors

explanation.surface: A question about what keeps a boarding house safe.
explanation.walkthrough: PAD is slang for lodgings and LOCKS are devices for securing, so the word splits into both halves of the clue as well as naming a lock.
explanation.definitionFit: Detachable locks with a shackle are fastening devices used to keep doors, gates and sheds shut.

clue.text: Going up? Going down ? This way

definitions.text: Going up? Going down ? This way

parts.words: Going up? Going down ? This way
parts.note: a lift attendant's call, but the direction meant is straight vertical, at right angles to the ground

explanation.surface: A lift operator calling out to passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: It sounds like a lift operator's patter, but both 'up' and 'down' describe a single vertical line.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving straight up or straight down is travelling upright at right angles to the horizontal.

clue.text: To be elegant, the young lady has pneumatic support

parts.note: a deb, or debutante, is a young lady entering society
being held up by air is to be on air

explanation.surface: A stylish girl riding on an air cushion or tyres.
explanation.walkthrough: DEB, short for debutante, a girl presented in high society, is followed by ON AIR, supported by air.
explanation.definitionFit: Debonair describes suave, courteous charm, the stylish manner of the well-bred.

clue.text: Frequently concerning X

parts.note: of can mean about or concerning, as in 'tales of adventure'
X is the Roman numeral ten

explanation.surface: Something said to relate regularly to a mysterious X.
explanation.walkthrough: X is ten in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something that happens many times.

clue.text: Measures for mixing sago with milk, right?

indicators.note: something set out for mixing is stirred together, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A recipe asks for quantities of sago and milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for mixing' rearranges SAGO, MILK and R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: Units of weight in the metric system are measures of mass.

clue.text: How an oarsman may have a bit of fishing to fall back on ?

definitions.text: How an oarsman may have a bit of fishing to fall back on ?

parts.words: How an oarsman may have a bit of fishing to fall back on
parts.note: a rower whose blade sticks in the water is jerked backwards, a mishap named as if a shellfish were caught

explanation.surface: A rower is said to keep angling as a backup career.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To fall back on' sounds like a reserve plan, but it is literal: a rower who mistimes a stroke falls backwards off the seat, which rowers call catching a crab.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowing slang for a mistimed stroke that leaves the oar stuck and the rower toppling backwards.

clue.text: Tax a mourning-ring

definitions.meaning: a charge levied for using a road or bridge
the slow ringing of a bell for a death

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a levy paid at a bridge or turnpike; the other is a bell sounded slowly at a funeral.

clue.text: Nicer ale freshly brewed for the Trust

indicators.note: beer that is freshly brewed has been made anew, so these letters are made into a new order

explanation.surface: A pub praises newly made beer brewed for a charity trust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'freshly brewed' rearranges NICER ALE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Trust as a noun is confidence placed in someone, a direct synonym of dependence.

clue.text: Some sign on, agents — the minority

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An instruction to a few agents to put their names down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' takes part of 'sigN ON, AGEnts'. 'The minority' looks like the smaller group, but here it means being under age.
explanation.definitionFit: Minority in law is the period before adulthood, the same legal infancy as being under full age.

clue.text: One Gentile returns as a Hindu ascetic

indicators.note: something that returns goes back the way it came, so this word is read from right to left

parts.note: goy is the Yiddish word for a Gentile
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A non-Jewish man comes back as a holy man of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns GOY into YOG, then I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A practitioner of yoga who lives austerely is a classic Hindu holy man.

clue.text: Borneo's wild man of the woods

definitions.text: Borneo's wild man of the woods

parts.words: Borneo's wild man of the woods
parts.note: the Malay name of this ape means person of the forest, and it lives on Borneo

explanation.surface: A traveller's tale of a feral forest dweller on Borneo.
explanation.walkthrough: The Malay words orang (person) and hutan (forest) give the name, so the clue is a translation.
explanation.definitionFit: The great red ape of Borneo and Sumatra carries a Malay name meaning forest person.

clue.text: Inside the cart there's an unusual view of the road

indicators.note: Inside says one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a dray is a low cart for heavy loads

indicators.note: an unusual version of the word view has its letters in a new order

explanation.surface: A passenger in a cart enjoys a strange view of the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' turns VIEW into IVEW, and 'Inside' puts that within DRAY.
explanation.definitionFit: A private road leading from the street up to a house is a short access road.

clue.text: Contemplated the face in the object

indicators.note: in places the face word inside the object word

parts.note: an end is an object or aim
a visage is a face

explanation.surface: Someone studied the face shown in an item.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts VISAGE inside END, end meaning aim or purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: To envisage is to picture in the mind, which is to have contemplated something.

clue.text: Kitchen flower-vase?

parts.note: a stock is a garden flower, so a pot holding one sounds like a vase, while cooks use the same name for a pan of broth

explanation.surface: Asking what vase a cook keeps flowers in.
explanation.walkthrough: Stocks are scented garden flowers, so a pot for them would be a flower-vase; in a kitchen the same name means a large pan for simmering broth.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep pan in which bones and vegetables are simmered for soup base.

clue.text: Attractive fabric in black art creation?

indicators.note: in places the fabric word inside the black art word

parts.note: black art is a name for magic
net is a mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A question whether some charming cloth was made by sorcery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts NET inside MAGIC; 'creation?' rounds off the picture of the fabric being made.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that draws iron towards it is literally attractive, and figuratively a charming person is too.

clue.text: It makes a pass of one's passport

definitions.text: It makes a pass of one's passport

parts.words: It makes a pass of one's passport
parts.note: an endorsement stamped in a travel document turns it into a permit to enter a country

explanation.surface: Something that converts a travel document into a licence to go through.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR added a stray '24'; the page prints none. 'Pass' looks like an amorous advance but is a permit to enter.
explanation.definitionFit: An entry permit stamped into a travel document authorises the holder to cross a border.

clue.text: He's far different again

indicators.note: made different, the letters of these words take a new order

explanation.surface: A man who is far away seems changed once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges HE'S FAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something anew, starting over from scratch, is doing it once more.

clue.text: Mushroom development of a cigar?

indicators.note: the development of something reshapes it, so these letters are formed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a cigar could grow into a fungus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' rearranges A CIGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A gill-bearing fungus, the family that includes the field mushroom.

clue.text: What old Thomas would have made of it, given time?

definitions.text: What old Thomas would have made of it, given time?

parts.words: What old Thomas would have made of it, given time
parts.note: Thomas the ..., a medieval Scottish poet, would pair the word 'it' or 'time' with a matching sound

explanation.surface: Wondering what an old man named Thomas would make of something with time.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Thomas is Thomas the Rhymer (Thomas of Erceldoune), a 13th-century Scottish seer and poet. 'Given time' hints at a word that chimes with 'time'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pairing of words with matching end sounds is what a poet called the Rhymer would produce.

clue.text: The actual measurement of vital statistics ?

definitions.text: The actual measurement of vital statistics ?

parts.words: The actual measurement of vital statistics
parts.note: vital statistics are bodily measurements, and taken at true scale they are as large as a living body

explanation.surface: Asking for someone's true bust, waist and hip figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vital' hints at life, so the statistics of a life give its full measurement: a likeness at true scale.
explanation.definitionFit: Something made at the same scale as the real thing matches its actual measurement.

clue.text: Like a belt going up to a pound an ounce

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A belt is said to be rising from a pound to an ounce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns L, AN and OZ (LANOZ) round, as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Zonal means arranged in bands, a zone originally being a girdle round the waist.

clue.text: Don't go, Guy

definitions.meaning: a plea to remain where you are
a guy is a rope bracing a mast or tent

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to remain; the other is a supporting rope, as on a ship's mast.

clue.text: An aeroplane's mechanical winepress?

parts.note: a machine for fortified wine from Oporto would be named for that wine, while a plane's left-hand motor bears the same name

explanation.surface: A fanciful gadget on a plane that squeezes wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Port is both a fortified wine and the left side of an aircraft, so a motor on that side reads as a wine machine.
explanation.definitionFit: The motor on the left side of an aircraft, port being the nautical and aviation word for left.

clue.text: What's my line? It's in my tree

definitions.text: What's my line? It's in my tree

parts.words: What's my line? It's in my tree
parts.note: a line here is a line of descent, recorded on a family tree

explanation.surface: Echoing a TV panel game about guessing jobs, with a hint involving a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's my line?' was a TV quiz about occupations; here 'line' means descent from forebears, shown on a family tree.
explanation.definitionFit: One's line of forebears is the lineage set out in a family tree.

clue.text: Crowd of 500-550 in colour

indicators.note: in places the numbers inside the colour word

parts.note: hue is a colour or shade
D is the Roman numeral 500 and DL is 550

explanation.surface: A crowd of five hundred or so people in uniform colours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D (500) and DL (550) inside HUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A huddle is a tightly packed group, a small crowd pressed together.
